1234	def _dim(name: str, dtype: str, values: List[Any], macro: Optional[str],
1235	         applies_to: List[str], kind: str = "macro") -> Dict[str, Any]:
1236	    """One tuning dimension.
1237	
1238	    ``kind`` is one of:
1239	      - ``"macro"`` (default): becomes a ``-DSG_TUNED_*=VAL`` flag passed to nvcc/hipcc.
1240	      - ``"pallas_kwarg"``: passed as a keyword argument to ``pl.pallas_call``.
1241	      - ``"nvcc_flag"`` / ``"hipcc_flag"``: promoted to a bare compiler flag
1242	        (handled out-of-band, e.g. ``maxrregcount``).
1243	    """
1244	    return {"name": name, "type": dtype, "values": values,
1245	            "macro": macro, "applies_to": applies_to, "kind": kind}
1246	
1247	
1248	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1249	# Live vs. dead tuning dimensions
1250	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1251	#
1252	# A producer→consumer audit of the emitted ``-DSG_TUNED_*`` macros against the
1253	# committed kernel bodies (grep of every *.cu / *.hip.cpp) showed that of the
1254	# ~22 macros the autotuner can emit, only FIVE are ever ``#ifdef``'d / read by
1255	# any kernel:
1256	#
1257	#   SG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE  (11 consumers)   — live
1258	#   SG_TUNED_VEC_WIDTH   (11 consumers)   — live
1259	#   SG_TUNED_UNROLL      (11 consumers)   — live
1260	#   SG_TUNED_ASYNC_DEPTH (12 consumers)   — live  (kernel clamps to [1,4])
1261	#   SG_TUNED_CLUSTER_SHAPE (2 consumers)  — live
1262	#
1263	# ``maxrregcount`` carries ``macro=None`` and is emitted as a real
1264	# ``--maxrregcount=N`` / ``-amdgpu-max-num-vgprs=N`` compiler flag, so it
1265	# genuinely changes the produced binary and is LIVE even though it is not an
1266	# SG_TUNED macro. All Pallas dims (kind == "pallas_kwarg") are real
1267	# ``pl.pallas_call`` arguments and are likewise LIVE.
1268	#
1269	# Every OTHER SG_TUNED_* / *_ENABLED macro (NUM_STAGES, SWIZZLE,
1270	# TMA_DESCRIPTORS, WGMMA_SHAPE, WARP_SPECIALIZATION, FP8/FP4_LAYOUT,
1271	# TCGEN05_VARIANT, LDS_PADDING, WAVES_PER_EU, MFMA_SHAPE, FP8/FP4_MFMA_LAYOUT,
1272	# SCHEDULER_HINT, WMMA_SHAPE, DPP_MODIFIER, TGSPLIT, the bare TMA bool) is
1273	# DEAD: no kernel reads it, so every distinct value produces a
1274	# binary-IDENTICAL artifact. Leaving these in the search space (a) inflates the
1275	# Cartesian product by ~10^4× on sm_90 / sm_100, wasting the sampler's trial
1276	# budget on binary-identical configs, and (b) poisons ``config_key`` so two
1277	# binary-identical configs hash to different keys → false cache misses → full
1278	# recompiles.
1279	#
1280	# We keep the macros *emittable* (the dims stay in the space, the
1281	# ``resolve_macros`` / ``resolve_extra_*_flags`` paths are untouched) so a dead
1282	# dim can be revived later by simply moving its name into ``_LIVE_TUNING_DIMS``.
1283	# But for now each dead dim is PINNED to a single default value (so it stops
1284	# expanding the search space) and DROPPED from ``config_key`` (so binary-
1285	# identical configs collapse to one cache entry).

Area: `grokking_optimizers/compile.py` search-space + the sm_90 TC megakernel launch path

## 0. One-paragraph summary

The kernel side of L2-persistence already exists and is committed:
`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/primitives.cuh:387` defines `L2PersistScope`, an RAII
wrapper over `cudaStreamSetAttribute` + `cudaAccessPolicyWindow` +
`cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, …)`, gated by

instantiated NOWHERE** (grep of `csrc/` + `grokking_optimizers/` finds only the
class body and the doc-comment example — no live construction). So the missing
pieces are exactly the two the task names:

* **(a)** a compile.py TUNED dim that parameterizes the window — a *hit-ratio*
  knob and a *set-aside size* (`cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize`) knob — emitted
  as `-DSG_TUNED_*` macros; and
* **(b)** wiring those macros through the launch path so `L2PersistScope` is
  actually constructed around the persistent megakernel launch, reading the
  tuned hit-ratio / set-aside instead of the hardcoded `hitRatio=1.0f` /
  span-derived limit it uses today.

The hard constraints (CPU-only here; gfx942/tpu_v6e preserved; transport-only
legal rewrites; fp64+A/A/A gate) are respected because: the dim defaults make
the canonical build **byte-identical** to today (window OFF / hitRatio 1.0 /
auto-span), the macro is **sm_90-only** and **device-target only** (HIP/TPU
spaces untouched), and L2 residency is a *cache hint* that **cannot change
numerical results** — it only changes which lines stay hot, so the fp64 +
determinism gate is structurally unaffected (still must be re-verified on
silicon per the keep/revert ratchet, but the rewrite is hint-only by
construction).

---

## 1. What the current code actually is (cited)

### 1.1 `L2PersistScope` — the committed kernel-side primitive

`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/primitives.cuh`:

* `383-385`: `#ifndef ENABLE_L2_PERSIST / #define ENABLE_L2_PERSIST 1`.
* `387-468`: `class L2PersistScope`. Ctor signature
  (`390-392`): `L2PersistScope(cudaStream_t stream, void* p0, size_t n0,
  void* p1 = nullptr, size_t n1 = 0)`.
* `405-408`: queries `cudaDevAttrMaxPersistingL2CacheSize`; no-op if `<= 0`.
* `411-421`: builds the smallest byte span covering `{p0,n0}∪{p1,n1}`; **no-op
  if `span > max_persist`** (the device's reservable persisting-L2).
* `424`: `cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, span)` — **today
  it reserves exactly `span`** (the whole buffer), not a tuned fraction.
* `426-436`: fills `cudaStreamAttrValue` — **`hitRatio = 1.0f` hardcoded
  (`429`)**, `hitProp = cudaAccessPropertyPersisting`, `missProp =
  cudaAccessPropertyStreaming`; `cudaStreamSetAttribute(... AccessPolicyWindow
  ...)`.
* `442-457`: dtor resets the window (num_bytes=0), `cudaCtxResetPersistingL2Cache()`,
  releases the carve-out (`SetLimit(…, 0)`).
* `463`: `bool active()`.

So the two TUNED knobs map cleanly onto two existing-but-hardcoded values:
`hitRatio` (`429`) and the `SetLimit` size (`424`). The class needs a **second
ctor overload** (or two extra defaulted args) carrying `(hit_ratio,
set_aside_bytes)`; default args reproduce today's behaviour exactly.

### 1.2 The launch site — where the scope must be constructed

`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh`:

* `1511-1515`: `template <OptId Opt> cudaError_t
  launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc(PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
  DecoderTokenCtx tok, float* grad, float lr, int step, FusedOptState st,

  launcher) gains `#ifndef SG_TUNED_L2_PERSIST_*` guards, the scanner sees the
  tokens and the dim auto-activates; until then it is auto-pinned to default →

  forward-compatible contract used by `dec_gemm_stages` et al.
  (`compile.py:2283-2294` + the comment `2275-2282`).
* `2122-2327`: `_sm90_full_space()` — the Hopper dim list. New dims go in the

  `mega_block` `2186`, `tile_m` `2217`): **first value == the in-header

  literal nvcc accepts).

`grokking_optimizers/compile.py:14888-14908` — `_tc_relevant_device_flags`:

This is an **explicit allowlist**: the real-TC build TU
(`_build_tc_real_step_module`, `14911`) is fed ONLY the macros in
`keep_macros`. **Every other device `-D` is dropped before it reaches the
megakernel TU.** So the new L2 macros MUST be added to `keep_macros` or they
will never reach `mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu` /
`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh`. This is the single most important wiring edit,
and the one easiest to miss.

* `14840-14855`: `_GEMM_TILE_DIM_NAMES` + `14868-14876`

---

## 2. Design decisions (and why)

### 2.1 Two knobs, generic / config-declared (NOT SuperGrok-hardcoded)

Per the task: a **hit-ratio** dim and a **set-aside size** dim. Both are
*portable* hardware concepts (`cudaAccessPolicyWindow.hitRatio`,
`cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize`), declared as ordinary `_dim(...)` entries in
the arch-generic `_sm90_full_space()` — no model name, no SuperGrok constant.

* **`l2_persist`** (bool, `SG_TUNED_L2_PERSIST`): master on/off. Default
  **`False`** → the launch wrapper compiles to a no-op (`if (false)` around the
  scope) → byte-identical to today (today the scope is never constructed at
  all). This is the keep/revert-safe default: the ratchet starts from OFF.
* **`l2_hit_ratio`** (the fraction of accesses in the window that get the
  persisting property — `0.0..1.0`). Macro `SG_TUNED_L2_HIT_RATIO`. Values
  `[1.0, 0.5, 0.75, 0.25]` — first value `1.0` == the hardcoded `hitRatio`
  at `primitives.cuh:429`, so when the window IS enabled the default reproduces
  the primitive's current literal. (Hardware: `hitRatio < 1.0` lets the policy
  probabilistically demote some lines so an over-large window doesn't thrash;
  it's the canonical NVIDIA L2-residency tuning axis.)
* **`l2_setaside_frac`** (fraction of `cudaDevAttrMaxPersistingL2CacheSize` to
  reserve via `cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, …)`). Macro
  `SG_TUNED_L2_SETASIDE_PCT`, integer percent to stay nvcc-`-D`-clean (no float
  in this one). Values `[100, 75, 50, 25]` — first `100` == today's behaviour
  (`primitives.cuh:424` reserves the full span, i.e. effectively up to the max).
  Expressed as a **percent of the device max**, not absolute bytes, so it is
  hardware-portable (an H100 has ~50 MB, a future part more — the percent
  scales). The launch wrapper computes `set_aside = max_persist * pct / 100`
  and passes it to the scope; the scope still clamps `span <= max_persist`.

Rationale for percent-of-max over absolute bytes: absolute bytes would bake an
H100 number into a portable config; percent keeps it device-agnostic and within
the existing `int` `-D` machinery (no float-literal emission needed for this
knob).

### 2.2 Why a bool gate + two value knobs (3 dims) and not one fused enum

Three orthogonal `_dim`s compose with `_pin_dead_dims` / `config_key` /

couple the on/off decision to the value grid and break the "first value ==

the host TU is untouched. **gfx942 / tpu_v6e preserved** by construction (no
edit to their builders; HIP has no `cudaAccessPolicyWindow`).

L2 residency is a pure **cache hint**: `cudaAccessPropertyPersisting` vs
`Streaming` changes only *which lines the hardware prefers to keep*, never the
values read/written. The ascending-k fp32 reduction order, the wgmma operand
order, every store — all identical. So this is a **transport-only legal
rewrite** in the project's sense (it preserves the exact byte sequence the
megakernel computes). The fp64(1e-4; SAM 2.5e-2) + A/A/A determinism gate is

the keep/revert ratchet for any non-default winner (the autotuner can't *prove*

change. The default (`l2_persist=False`) is a literal no-op, so the gate is
